title: OPT window is open
ask: Have you asked your DSO for the OPT recommendation and filed Form I-765 online within 30 days of the new I-20, and before 60 days after your program end date?
why: USCIS accepts post-completion OPT applications from 90 days before to 60 days after the program end date. Missing the 30-day or 60-day deadline means a denial.

title: Program has ended
ask: Your 60-day OPT filing window and grace period are running. Is your I-765 filed, or do you have another plan (new program, change of status, departure) before day 60?
why: After 60 days past the program end date you can no longer apply for OPT and your grace period is over.

title: On OPT
ask: Do you have an SEVP Portal account, with your current employer and address reported there within 10 days of any change?
why: Unreported employment counts as unemployment, and 90 days of unemployment on OPT (150 with STEM) ends your status.

links.label: SEVP Portal help (Study in the States)

title: Unemployment days running low
ask: You have 45 or fewer unemployment days left. Is each job at least 20 hours a week, related to your degree, and reported in the SEVP Portal?
why: Post-completion OPT allows 90 days of unemployment in total; STEM OPT adds 60 more. Going over ends your F-1 status automatically.

title: OPT EAD expires within 90 days
ask: If your degree's CIP code is on the STEM list and your employer uses E-Verify, have you and your employer signed the I-983 and filed the STEM OPT I-765 before your current EAD expires?
why: A timely filed STEM extension gives you an automatic 180-day work extension while USCIS decides. Filing after the EAD expires is not possible.

links.label: STEM designated degree list (Study in the States)

title: On STEM OPT
ask: Do you know your next I-983 dates: the 12-month evaluation, the final evaluation, and the 6-month validation reports to your DSO? Any employer change needs a new I-983 within 10 days.
why: Missed evaluations and reports are the most common STEM OPT violations, and they surface later at the H-1B or green-card stage.

links.label: STEM OPT hub (Study in the States)

title: H-1B registration season
ask: Is your employer registering you in this year's H-1B lottery, and do they know the offered wage level now weights your odds (Level IV counts four times, Level I once)?
why: Registration runs for about two weeks in March. Under the weighted-selection rule used from the FY2027 season, a higher wage level materially improves selection chances.

title: Travelling outside the US
ask: Is the travel signature on page 2 of your I-20 less than 12 months old (6 months if you are on OPT or STEM OPT), and if on OPT will you carry your EAD card and a job letter?
why: Without a recent DSO signature CBP can refuse entry or send you to secondary inspection; on OPT officers expect proof of employment.

links.label: Travel on F-1 (Study in the States)

title: OPT ending
ask: Your 60-day grace period runs from the EAD end date. Do you have a plan: SEVIS transfer to a new program, change of status (H-4, H-1B, B-2), or departure before it ends?
why: The grace period allows preparation to leave or a transfer, not work. Staying past it starts unlawful presence.
